title: spec review: S2e worker_control.cancel: safe cancellation of a running worker with worktree and commits preserved, structured partial result, registry and bus updated, capacity released (P15, P16)
spec:
Create orchestrator/worker_control.py. cancel(task_id, reason, *, source="planner", grace_s=20) -> dict: registry status cancelling (event cancel_requested with reason and source); signal the worker process: for claude workers the registry pid (SIGTERM, then SIGKILL after grace_s if still alive); for codex workers executor.py must record the codex exec subprocess pid in the registry at launch (edit executor.py: the Popen or run call that starts codex exec; pass the pid to worker_registry.upsert) so cancel can signal it the same way; never touch the worktree files; collect partial = partial_result(task) -> {files_changed: git status --porcelain paths in the worktree, diff_stat: git diff --stat against the task base (merge-base with the goal branch), commits: log of commits since the base (sha, subject), tests_run: the last gate output lines in the worktree if scripts/failures_only.sh output or a tests-green log exists, else [], errors: last 20 lines of the worker's stderr capture if the registry exit event kept a path, files_inspected: paths from registry tool events when present, unresolved: []} — observable evidence only, never prompt or transcript text; bus: bus.update(task_id, status="held", hold_reason="cancelled", pid=None, result={"partial": partial, "cancel_reason": reason, "cancelled_by": source, "confidence": 0.0, "provenance": ["worker_partial"]}) (check bus.STATUSES and post_result size cap; truncate lists to fit); pool release: pool.Pool().release(task_id, {}) as executor.py does; registry finish cancelled; return the partial. daemon.auto_fix_round must skip held tasks whose hold_reason is cancelled (they are the Planner's to re-spec) and reconcile_dead must not requeue a task whose registry status is cancelling or cancelled. CLI: `orchestrator workers cancel <task> --reason <text>` prints the partial summary. Docs: docs/hermes-hardening/11-worker-control.md (cancel sequence, what is preserved, what is never captured).
Repository rules: unittest (not pytest), tests/_harness.py single ORCH_ROOT fixture; every acceptance test id tests/test_<module>.py::test_name is a method def test_name(self) in a unittest.TestCase. No new third-party dependencies. Never write secret values to any file or log; test fixtures use synthetic names and values that are not credential-shaped. Do not quote template placeholder tokens (double braces) anywhere in code comments or docs. Shadow-first: a new adaptive path never changes what a worker sees until its mode is active; shadow only writes decision_log or runs rows. Run .claude/hooks/tests-green.sh . until green; the base suite must stay green. Do not ask questions: decide, and note decisions in the result summary. The interface contracts of the stage 1 modules are in .orchestrator/plan.md (section GOAL T-0991) and in docs/hermes-hardening/0*.md on this branch; read the merged module before building on it.
acceptance: tests/test_worker_control.py::test_cancel_signals_process_preserves_worktree_and_holds_task (fake process, temp worktree with an uncommitted change and one commit: worktree untouched, status held cancelled, partial lists the change and the commit, registry cancelled, pool released)
tests/test_worker_control.py::test_partial_result_contains_only_observable_evidence (no key named prompt, packet, transcript, reasoning)

risks.issue: cancel() is specced to log 'event cancel_requested with reason and source', but worker_registry.event() whitelists KINDS (no 'cancel_requested') and FIELDS (no 'source'; only 'status_reason' exists for reason text). worker_registry.py is not in scope, so as written this call raises ValueError before cancel() ever signals the process.

`workers` is currently a flat subparser with --task/--all/--json, not a subcommand group. `orchestrator workers cancel <task> --reason <text>` requires restructuring it into nested subparsers; the spec doesn't say how to do this without breaking the existing `workers --task/--all` invocation.

reconcile_dead(t, pool) receives a snapshot taken by tick()'s `bus.read(status='running')` before cancel() flips the task to held; if cancel() runs concurrently with a tick, reconcile_dead's own held/post_result calls can overwrite cancel's hold_reason='cancelled' and partial result. The spec's guard ('reconcile_dead must not requeue a task whose registry status is cancelling or cancelled') should be an explicit worker_registry status check inside reconcile_dead itself, not an assumption that bus status alone prevents the race.

grace_s=20 escalation (SIGTERM then SIGKILL) doesn't specify how the wait is implemented; a literal time.sleep(grace_s) makes test_cancel_escalates_to_kill_after_grace slow (~20s) and couples the test to real time unless the spec calls for an injectable clock/poll seam.

suggested_spec_changes: Replace the 'event cancel_requested with reason and source' step with either (a) worker_registry.upsert(task_id, status='cancelling', status_reason=f'{reason} (source={source})') using existing fields only, or (b) add orchestrator/worker_registry.py to scope and extend KINDS with 'cancel_requested' and FIELDS with 'source', documenting that as an explicit interface change.

Specify the exact `workers` CLI restructuring: e.g. convert `workers` into a subparser group with a default 'list' behavior (preserving --task/--all/--json) plus a new 'cancel' subcommand taking a positional task and required --reason, so the executor doesn't have to guess how to preserve backward compatibility.

Add an explicit instruction that reconcile_dead() must check worker_registry.get(t['id'])['status'] in ('cancelling','cancelled') and return early, rather than relying solely on bus status having already changed.

Specify that cancel()'s grace period wait must be implemented via an injectable/mockable sleep or poll function (or accept a max poll count) so test_cancel_escalates_to_kill_after_grace does not require a real ~20s wait.
